title: Exactness of the constructed kernel boundary
statement: For every commutative ring R, modules M,F,N and surjective q:F → N, the map δ_q of [def-sc-p1-tor-kernel-boundary-construction] satisfies exactness of (Tor₁(q,M),δ_q) and (δ_q,inclusion tensor 1_M). This makes no naturality assertion.

proof.text: Resolve 0 → ker(q) → F → N → 0 by degreewise split free resolutions using [lem-weil-pbc-free-resolution-ses-split]. Tensor with M and apply [lem-weil-pbc-complex-ses-homology-long-exact] to obtain the two exact pairs adjacent to the homology boundary.

Compare the chosen projective resolution P of N with the right horseshoe resolution by [lem-weil-pbc-tor-map-via-resolution-lift]. Lift the degree-zero comparison through the split middle term. Its augmentation e₀:P₀ → F lifts ε. The snake cycle formula identifies the horseshoe boundary with (e₀d₁) tensor 1, with codomain restricted to the kernel. The difference e-e₀ factors through a map k:P₀ → ker(q); its boundary contribution (kd₁) tensor 1 vanishes on cycles. Hence this is exactly the map of [def-sc-p1-tor-kernel-boundary-construction]. Identify H₀ with tensor using [lem-weil-pbc-tensor-right-exact], and transport the exact pairs. This comparison proves exactness of the fixed construction without assuming arbitrary exact boundaries are natural.

theorem tor_kernel_boundary_construction_exact
    (R : Type u) [CommRing R] (M : ModuleCat.{u} R)
    (F N : ModuleCat.{u} R) (q : F →ₗ[R] N) (hq : Function.Surjective q) :
    Function.Exact (((Tor' (ModuleCat.{u} R) 1).map
      (ModuleCat.ofHom q)).app M).hom (torKernelBoundary M F N q hq) ∧
    Function.Exact (torKernelBoundary M F N q hq)
      ((LinearMap.ker q).subtype.rTensor M)
